about.title: San Fernando Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in San Fernando often involve local urgent care clinics, community hospitals, and specialists serving the surrounding Los Angeles County population. These claims are different from other injury matters because California's MICRA law layers on specific requirements: a strict notice period before filing, tight timing rules tied to when the harm was discovered, and a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts annually. Not every disappointing medical result qualifies as malpractice — the law requires proof that a provider deviated from an accepted standard of care and that deviation caused real harm. That distinction matters, and it's typically established through a qualified medical expert's review of the records. If you believe a delay, misdiagnosis, surgical error, or medication mistake caused harm to you or a family member in San Fernando, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can review what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Most Under California's MICRA Rules

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the harm, but never more than three years from the actual injury. On top of that, a 90-day written notice must go to the provider before any lawsuit is filed, so timing missteps can cost you your claim.

items.title: A Cap That Changes Annually
items.desc: MICRA sets a limit on non-economic damages, but that cap is not frozen — it rises each year under the current law. An attorney familiar with the current figure can explain how it may apply to your situation.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad outcome by itself isn't evidence of malpractice under California law. Cases typically need a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached and that the breach caused the harm.

items.question: I had a bad outcome at a hospital near San Fernando — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard and that this failure caused your injury. A poor result alone, even a serious one, doesn't automatically meet that bar, which is why medical record review is usually the first step.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim after a medical error in San Fernando?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California's MICRA law caps non-economic damages, though that cap increases each year under current rules. An independent attorney can walk you through how the current cap and other factors might apply to your specific claim.
